subject: Following up on our meeting
body:
Hi Micah,

I hope you are doing well.

I have discussed the implementation of well-being report distribution for the Matter project with the team and wanted to share our findings.

We have two options to consider:
  1. Adding a survey in the app that includes custom URLs for participants in an informational question. This option can be implemented relatively quickly, but it has certain limitations. Participants need to be enrolled first, and then we can attach links with their Avicenna IDs. Additionally, participants will have to leave the app to review the link and then return to click the "Submit" button to access the app's home page.
  2. Adding a page activity that sends custom URLs to each participant. This approach is more intuitive because it will be hosted inside the app. However, it would take approximately two weeks to implement, and the app would require an update.
Please note that we assumed the participant ID refers to their Avicenna IDs. If not, we can only proceed with the first option and will need you to provide the IDs as a CSV file. While both options require some customization, we are happy to offer them at no extra cost. We highly recommend using the Avicenna IDs and choosing the second option if possible, as it will greatly enhance the user experience. However, please let me know your preference, and we will proceed accordingly.

Best,
Sara

Amin Tavassolian Just to be sure, the answer to the following question is no, correct? This page activity will be available on the app in approximately two weeks, allowing enrolled participants to view the well-being report, and won't affect the study at all.
> If we went with number #2 and it two weeks to implement, would it cause complications for users who are already enrolled in the study and responding to surveys when we launch that feature?

Sara Farnya 
> This page activity will be available on the app in approximately two weeks, allowing enrolled participants to view the well-being report, and won't affect the study at all.

This is correct.

>  If we went with number #2 and it two weeks to implement, would it cause complications for users who are already enrolled in the study and responding to surveys when we launch that feature?

No, the only thing they need to do is to update the app. Everything else would be seamless.

Amin Tavassolian Thanks a lot.

> No, the only thing they need to do is to update the app. Everything else would be seamless.

Sorry, when you say "updating the app," do you mean reloading the devices or resubmitting the app to the store?

Sara Farnya We need to send an update to the app store and participants need to update their apps. The app update on the participant side works in 2 ways: 1- Most ppl turn on auto-update option in iPhones so this happens automatically and seamlessly for these ppl, 99% of ppl do this. 2- If they disable this option, they need to install the new version manually. 
Regardless, when a new version is installed, the study update itself in the very first launch.
